question: What economic policies did Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi propose in 2025?
text:
In 2025, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi proposed what she called **“responsible and proactive” fiscal policy**: use government spending and tax relief to ease the cost-of-living squeeze, while investing with the private sector to raise wages and strengthen long-term growth. She laid out the approach in her October 24 policy speech, and her Cabinet approved a **¥21.3 trillion stimulus package** on November 21. ([japan.kantei.go.jp](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/104/statement/202510/24shoshinhyomei.html?bsft_aaid=72bb9dec-3452-4075-a63c-0f8d60246a1e&bsft_clkid=6c18bd80-303b-4b98-82b0-10f2840e1d39&bsft_eid=a30f775d-a95b-4704-ba5b-9fcd5291f465&bsft_ek=2026-02-16T05%3A00%3A34Z&bsft_lx=6&bsft_mid=90fc3602-ddfd-451c-96a8-cc6e033e1f1c&bsft_mime_type=html&bsft_tv=1285&bsft_txnid=e39b4aa0-5748-470d-98fc-2b389a8e2054&bsft_uid=54e33523-d5da-4f6c-adb8-c5cdeb30b16d&bsft_utid=54e33523-d5da-4f6c-adb8-c5cdeb30b16d-Newsletter_COR_WHATEVERITTAKES&utm_source=openai))

Her main proposals were:

- **Cut household costs.** Scrap the provisional gasoline and diesel tax surcharges, subsidize winter electricity and gas bills, provide extra payments to families with children, and give local governments funds to help residents cope with higher food prices. ([mof.go.jp](https://www.mof.go.jp/english/policy/budget/budget/fy2025/03.pdf?utm_source=openai))
- **Raise take-home pay.** Raise the minimum taxable income threshold to **¥1.78 million** in the fiscal 2026 tax plan, begin designing a refundable tax credit for low- and middle-income earners, and help small businesses afford wage increases. Her October coalition agreement also called for considering a **two-year suspension of the consumption tax on qualifying food and beverages**; that was not part of the November stimulus. ([mof.go.jp](https://www.mof.go.jp/english/policy/tax_policy/tax_reform/08keyhighlight.pdf?utm_source=openai))
- **Invest in strategic industries and economic security.** Direct public and private investment toward areas such as AI, semiconductors, shipbuilding, quantum technology, and space, while strengthening critical supply chains, energy and food security, and disaster preparedness. ([japan.kantei.go.jp](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/ongoingtopics/sogokeizaitaisaku2025/index.html?utm_source=openai))

The Diet passed a separate **¥18.3 trillion supplementary budget** on December 16 to fund much of the package. The two figures measure different things: the broader stimulus total also counted measures such as tax cuts. ([japan.kantei.go.jp](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/104/statement/202511/21kaiken.html?utm_source=openai))
